recipes.title: Muffin-Tin Meal Prep Beef Meatballs
steps: Weigh
Zero a bowl on a kitchen scale, add the beef, vegetables and seasonings, and note the total weight so you can divide it evenly by the days you're prepping for.
Mix & portion
Mix well, then weigh out 2–2¼ oz portions and roll into meatballs (about 3 make a 6 oz serving).
Bake in a mini muffin tin

Place one meatball in each cup of a mini muffin pan; they cook in their own juices, stay round and cook faster. Bake at 420°F (215°C) for 10–12 minutes (broil the last 2 minutes if you like), and don't overcook.
Use through the week
Simmer in marinara, crumble over salads, or serve as an after-school snack; one 2 oz meatball is a good kid-sized portion.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; full recipes are on the creator's site. Weighing everything is the creator's "exact meal prep" method for counting calories accurately.

recipes.title: Three-Flavor Sheet Pan Chicken Bites (meal prep)

items.i: boneless skinless chicken breast, trimmed and cut into nickel-size pieces
liquid aminos or low-sodium soy sauce
arrowroot starch (1 tsp for chicken, 1 tsp for sauce)

steps: Pat dry
Cut the chicken into small bite-size pieces, then pat very dry and let it sit on paper towels a few minutes, especially if it was frozen, so the seasoning sticks.
Base season
Toss with the onion and garlic powder, weigh it, and divide into three equal bowls.
Flavor

Bowl 1: chili powder, cumin and cilantro. Bowl 2: five-spice, aminos and sesame oil. Bowl 3: toss with 1 tsp arrowroot, then coat with the Dijon, agave, water and another 1 tsp arrowroot mixed together.
Make the pan
Line a sheet pan with foil (or parchment) and pinch up two ridges to make three sections so the juices don't mix.
Bake
Spread one flavor in each section in a single layer and bake at 420°F (215°C) for 12–15 minutes; the small pieces cook fast.
Portion
Weigh out portions for the week; leftovers work in chicken salad, frittatas or soup.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; full recipes are on the creator's site. Small pieces cook faster and stay easier to eat even if slightly overcooked.
